title: Treat erectile dysfunction with an effective oral PDE5 inhibitor

concept.text: Enable erections sufficient for sexual activity through an oral medicine, replacing more invasive treatment for many patients. This is symptomatic treatment; it does not establish restoration of untreated erectile function. Proposed completion test: FDA approval for adult ED based on placebo-controlled clinical trials demonstrating improved erection attainment and maintenance on validated questionnaires and intercourse outcomes. Test set by: FDA; the sildenafil approval and prescribing information specify the indication and clinical evidence. Reported achieved: FDA approved sildenafil (Viagra) on 27 March 1998. Sources given: [Original FDA Viagra approval letter](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/appletter/1998/20895ltr.pdf) ; [FDA Viagra prescribing information](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/020895s048lbl.pdf).

page.title: Oral PDE5 inhibition for erectile dysfunction
page.definition: An oral medicine inhibits phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5), an enzyme that breaks down a signal relaxing penile erectile tissue, and improves the ability to obtain and maintain erections sufficient for intercourse during sexual stimulation. This treats erectile dysfunction during medicine use.

goal.need: In the Massachusetts Male Aging Study, 847 men without erectile dysfunction at baseline were followed for an average 8.8 years. Incidence was 25.9 cases per 1,000 man-years (95% confidence interval 22.5–29.9). Baseline interviews occurred in 1987–1989 and follow-up in 1995–1997. Oral treatment targets difficulty obtaining or maintaining erections sufficient for intercourse.

figures.caption: Incidence of erectile dysfunction by age at study entry
figures.note: The analysis included 847 Massachusetts men without erectile dysfunction at baseline; these are incidence rates, not prevalence estimates.

completion.title: FDA approves an oral PDE5 inhibitor for the treatment of erectile dysfunction.
completion.criterion: FDA approves a new drug application for a medicine taken by mouth whose labelled mechanism is inhibition of phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5) and whose labelled indication is the treatment of erectile dysfunction. The approval rests on at least two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in men with erectile dysfunction of organic, psychogenic or mixed cause, whose primary endpoints are the International Index of Erectile Function questions on achieving erections sufficient for intercourse and on maintaining them after penetration. The first such approval meets the test. Injected, intraurethral and topical medicines, and use outside an approved indication, do not count.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration: approval of NDA 20-895 and the approved prescribing information for Viagra (sildenafil citrate), sections 1 and 14, which state the mechanism class, indication, trial design and primary endpoints.
completion.threshold_quote: VIAGRA is a phosphodiesterase-5 (PDE5) inhibitor indicated for the treatment of erectile dysfunction (ED)
completion.basis: The test is the regulator's approval, not an Atlas threshold, and it is the first approval of the mechanism class for this indication. The endpoints are those the label names as primary in the principal studies; the label reports 21 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in more than 3,000 patients. The indication is treatment while the medicine is used, with a dose taken as needed before sexual activity. The test does not require erectile function restored without the medicine.

milestones.title: A PDE5 inhibitor's laboratory results support reasonably safe human testing for erectile dysfunction.
milestones.criterion: Animal or in vitro pharmacology and toxicology studies of an oral PDE5 inhibitor support the sponsor's conclusion that the proposed clinical investigations are reasonably safe, and an investigational new drug application for it is in effect at FDA, which permits clinical investigation in the United States. Evidence of enzyme selectivity alone, or an effective application with no report of the supporting studies, is partial.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8), the general preclinical requirement for investigational drugs
milestones.threshold_quote: on the basis of which the sponsor has concluded that it is reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations.

milestones.title: An oral PDE5 inhibitor increases penile rigidity versus placebo in men with erectile dysfunction.
milestones.criterion: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in men with erectile dysfunction shows that an oral PDE5 inhibitor increases penile rigidity during sexual stimulation, measured by an instrument and not by questionnaire, compared with placebo (P < 0.05), and reports adverse events in each group. This is the preliminary evidence of effectiveness that precedes expanded trials. An uncontrolled study, or one in men without erectile dysfunction, is partial.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(b)–(c), preliminary clinical effectiveness before expanded trials; the rigidity assay was specified by the Pfizer–Southmead study
milestones.threshold_quote: after preliminary evidence suggesting effectiveness of the drug has been obtained

milestones.title: Pivotal trials establish erection and intercourse benefits and safety sufficient for prescribing.
milestones.criterion: At least two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of at-home treatment lasting at least 12 weeks, in men with erectile dysfunction, each show improvement over placebo (P < 0.05) on the International Index of Erectile Function questions on achieving and on maintaining erections, report the proportion of successful attempts at intercourse in each group, and report adverse events by frequency, as needed to assess benefit and risk and to write physician labelling. One such trial is partial.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(c); sildenafil efficacy endpoints are identified in section 14 of the approved prescribing information
milestones.threshold_quote: to provide an adequate basis for physician labeling.

not_found: No PDE5-specific numerical preclinical pass threshold was found in the FDA regulations, approval letter or prescribing information.
The 1998 FDA joint clinical review had no readable text; its individual preclinical study results and cohort sizes could not be verified.
The full 1992 NIH consensus statement and the 2018 AUA erectile dysfunction guideline could not be opened.

results.finding: Viagra (sildenafil citrate): sample size not reported; FDA verified that its IND became effective January 8, 1995.
results.detail: The effective IND is documented, but the notice reports no supporting animal or in vitro pharmacology or toxicology studies.
results.quote:
FDA has verified the applicant's claim that the date 
the investigational new drug application became effective was on 
January 8, 1995.

results.finding: FDA-approved oral sildenafil for erectile dysfunction: more than 3,000 treated patients across 21 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials.
results.detail: The FDA label establishes oral administration, PDE5 inhibition and the erectile dysfunction indication. Principal studies used the required IIEF primary endpoints: achieving erections sufficient for intercourse and maintaining erections after penetration.
results.quote:
VIAGRA was
 evaluated primarily at doses of 25 mg, 50 mg and 100 mg in 21 randomized, double-blind,
placebo-controlled trials of up to 6 months in duration, using a variety of study designs (fixed
dose, titration, parallel, crossover).
